P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No. As an EU member state, Italy applies Article 63 TFEU, which prohibits restrictions on capital movements and payments between EU countries and with non-EU countries. Banks still apply AML/KYC checks and may ask for the source of funds.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Self-employed people open a partita IVA (VAT number) with the Agenzia delle Entrate (opening fees not captured). Under the regime forfettario (flat-rate regime), revenues up to EUR 85,000 are taxed with a 15% substitute tax, or 5% for the first five years of a genuinely new activity (no partita IVA in the previous three years, not continuing previous work). Above EUR 85,000 you leave the regime the following year (immediately at EUR 100,000, per sources). INPS contributions are separate.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: The standard VAT rate is 22%. National: Italy has no general turnover exemption, since anyone making taxable supplies must register (Deloitte 2026). However, sole traders in the regime forfettario (previous-year revenue or fees up to EUR 85,000; see L7) do not charge VAT (Informazione Fiscale; Diritto.it). Exceeding EUR 100,000 during the year ends the regime immediately (search summary). Where services are taxed (EU-wide rules, illustrated by Irish Revenue guidance): (1) B2B, meaning services to business customers in other EU countries or outside the EU, are taxed where the customer is established, so no Italy VAT is charged; EU business customers self-account under the reverse charge. (2) B2C services to private individuals are, as a rule, taxed where the supplier is established, so Italy VAT applies once you are VAT-registered. (3) Exception: consultancy, legal, accounting, engineering, data-processing, advertising, licensing and electronically supplied services to private customers outside the EU are outside EU VAT, subject to 'use and enjoyment' rules. Electronically supplied services to private customers in other EU countries follow special OSS rules (not captured here).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies directly in Italy, supervised by the national data protection authority. It covers EU businesses and non-EU businesses offering goods or services to people in the EU.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: EU consumer law gives a 14-day withdrawal right for online and distance purchases without justification: 14 days from delivery for goods, and from conclusion of the contract for services. Exceptions include personalised goods, perishables and date-specific services.

sources.title: Returns and the right of withdrawal (Your Europe)
sources.quote: For goods this means 14 days from the date of delivery, for services 14 days after the day the contract was agreed.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Regime forfettario (2026, Budget Law 2026 art. 1 c. 27). Eligible if the previous year's revenue/fees, annualised, did not exceed EUR 85,000. Taxable income is revenue times a profitability coefficient set by ATECO code, and the substitute tax is 15%, or 5% for the first five years of a new activity meeting start-up conditions. Other 2026 conditions: employment or pension income no more than EUR 35,000 (extended to 2026), staff costs no more than EUR 20,000, no stakes in partnerships or professional associations. Non-residents qualify only if resident in the EU/EEA and at least 75% of their income is produced in Italy. In the opening year, the EUR 85,000 limit is pro-rated by days of activity.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (7) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
